# F13 and F14, and the one rule that would have caught both

The second review returned the ticket on two medium findings, and both are the first
review's F2 again in a different place: a figure that does not match the record it
names. F14 is fixed here. F13 cannot be fixed here, and the reason matters.

## F14, fixed

The Outcome's hook row said "837ms over 58 staged paths". Check 223's output says
"Checked 34 files in 316ms" and "46 modules, 67 dependencies cruised" and nothing
else: the 58 came from `git diff --cached --name-only` against the throwaway index
in `.harness-drafts/`, which is gitignored and does not survive the checkout. The row
now carries only what the check it cites can be read to say. The bar the Outcome sets
two sentences above that table is that a figure names the check it was read from, and
a figure whose check does not contain it fails that bar whether or not the number is
true.

## F13, which is why this ticket is at tdd again

Record 228 is an accepted tdd record and is append-only, so its narration cannot be
corrected: the fix is the next tdd record, written with the counts read out of the
checks it cites rather than from memory. Three of the six rounds were wrong, not two.
The reviewer found the first two and the third turned up while verifying them:

| round | the record said | the cited red actually ran |
|---|---|---|
| slice 2 | three of its hundred and two | red 213, 58 tests |
| slice 4 | 29 errors and 2 failures in 716 tests | red 217, 723 tests |
| the findings round | seven failures in 158 tests | red 221, 174 tests |

In all three the failing counts and the failing test names are right, which is why
four reviews passed over them: what is wrong is only the denominator, and the
denominator is what a reader uses to tell this slice's breakage from silent extra
breakage.

**The rule, which is F13's own candidate and is worth writing before the next ticket
needs it.** `harness/tdd-record-count-matches-check`: a failure_reason naming a test
total that the check it cites does not contain is a refusal at the tdd gate. The gate
already holds the record's `red` and `green` to the checks they name; holding a number
in the prose to the same check is the same comparison one layer in, and it is cheap:
the counts are in the recorded output. Every round of this ticket wrote that prose by
hand from a summary it had already read, which is exactly the shape of mistake a rule
should take off a reviewer's desk. It is the fourth finding of this ticket whose
candidate is about a figure and its record, after F2 and F14, and three of one kind is
what the weekly report's recurrence list exists to say out loud.

## What the next round does, in order

1. Replay the six pairs in attempt 11. The ticket file moved, so every pair in record
   228 is a citation against a tree that has changed; `.harness-drafts/replay2.sh`
   does the five, and the sixth is the mutation round, `scratchpad/mutate.py` plus
   reverting the registry entry and the `rules/fixtures/` exclusion.
2. Re-take the three measurements the Outcome's table cites, in this order so the
   numbers are to hand: the staged run, the tree run, `rules --check`.
3. Write the tdd record **with every count copied out of the check it cites**, and
   check each one against the record before advancing. The three rows above are the
   three to get right.
4. Set `status: review`, tick the five boxes, repoint the Outcome's figures at this
   attempt's checks, and only then run the regression and the coverage, in that order.
5. `harness review triage`, then the reviewer subagent on whatever the triage settles.

Twelve findings from the first review and two from the second are closed or placed,
and the rule set itself has not been questioned by either reviewer: all twenty-three
entries cross-check in both directions, every fixture is a genuine violation of its
own rule, and the second reviewer verified the first review's closures against the
checks rather than against their descriptions. What is left is bookkeeping, and the
bookkeeping is what has returned this ticket five times.
